question: Who is an unpaid seller under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930? Explain the rights of an unpaid seller against the goods.

points.label: Meaning of unpaid seller
points.description: A seller is unpaid when the whole price has not been paid or tendered, or when a bill of exchange or other negotiable instrument received as conditional payment has been dishonoured.

points.label: Right of lien
points.description: The seller in possession may retain the goods until paid, where goods are sold without credit, the credit period has expired, or the buyer becomes insolvent.

points.label: Stoppage in transit
points.description: Where the buyer becomes insolvent and the goods are in transit, the seller may resume possession and retain them until paid.

points.label: Right of resale
points.description: The seller may resell where the goods are perishable, or after giving notice of intention to resell if the buyer does not pay within a reasonable time, or where the right is expressly reserved.

points.label: Withholding delivery
points.description: Where property in the goods has not passed to the buyer, the unpaid seller may withhold delivery, similar to lien and stoppage in transit.
